misconfig_patterns: Security plugin disabled (xpack.security.enabled=false / OpenSearch security disabled) leaves GET /_snapshot and /_snapshot/{repo}/_all reachable unauthenticated — enumerates repository names, backend type, and each snapshot's indices[] array

AI-scope discriminator: a snapshot is in AI scope only if the cluster/snapshot holds vector or ML data. Confirm NAMES ONLY, no restore: (1) /_snapshot/{repo}/_all indices[] flags AI/ML-named indices (*embeddings*, *vectors*, *-knn, *rag*, *semantic*, *.ml-*, .ml-anomalies, .ml-config, .inference, *elser*); (2) GET /{index}/_mapping for field types dense_vector / sparse_vector / OpenSearch knn_vector (+ index.knn:true) and ELSER/inference fields = positive AI confirmation; (3) GET /_ingest/pipeline or /_ml/trained_models (ES) / /_plugins/_ml/models (OpenSearch) reveals deployed embedding/inference models. Absence of all three = generic substrate (text/log backup), OUT of scope. The snapshot manifest gives index names; the mapping read upgrades 'named like AI' to 'is AI vector store'.

Restraint: names-and-metadata only. Listing repositories, snapshot names, snapshot indices[], and field-type mappings is enumeration and is allowed. FORBIDDEN: POST .../_restore (write primitive that mutates the cluster), POST /_snapshot (registers/overwrites a repository = write), and any download/stream of the underlying repository object (fs path, S3/GCS/Azure bucket from settings) = exfiltration. The index/snapshot names ARE the finding. Surface open without exercised access stays 'surface open, access not exercised'.

passive: "You Know, for Search" port:9200 "cluster_name" -"security_exception" -"missing authentication credentials"

response_markers: GET /_snapshot returns JSON keyed by repo name with "type":"fs"|"s3"|"gcs"|"azure"|"url" and "uuid"+"settings"
OpenSearch fork tell: root JSON "version":{"distribution":"opensearch"} and .opensearch-* / .opendistro-* system indices in snapshot indices[]
active_probe.false_positive_check: http.title-style dorks over-match (9200 also hosts unrelated Java/HTTP apps and reverse proxies) — require the JSON markers "tagline":"You Know, for Search" + "cluster_uuid", not just port:9200. Auth-ENABLED clusters return 401 {"error":{"type":"security_exception","reason":"missing authentication credentials..."}} — exclude with -"security_exception" -"missing authentication credentials" (surface open, access not exercised). LBot/catch-all decoys echo ES banners — verify with a structural read: /_snapshot must return a JSON object keyed by repo names with real "type"+"uuid" and /_cluster/health must return {"status":...,"number_of_nodes":N}; a static/identical body across hosts = honeypot. Amazon OpenSearch Service managed domains front IAM/SigV4 and return AccessDenied/403 — exclude AWS ASNs / *.es.amazonaws.com. Kibana/OpenSearch-Dashboards on 5601 is the UI, not the data API. A snapshot present does NOT mean AI data present (gate via the discriminator).

shodan_dorks.strict: "You Know, for Search" port:9200 "cluster_name" -"security_exception" -"missing authentication credentials"

deployment_tells: GET / banner with tagline 'You Know, for Search' + cluster_name + cluster_uuid (version.distribution=opensearch for the fork)
GET /_snapshot returns JSON keyed by repo name with type fs/s3/gcs/azure/url + uuid + settings
GET /_snapshot/{repo}/_all returns snapshots[] with indices[] arrays and state SUCCESS/PARTIAL/FAILED
pivot_paths: GET / -> confirm banner: name, cluster_name, cluster_uuid, version.number, tagline 'You Know, for Search' (and version.distribution=opensearch for the fork)
GET /_cluster/health -> {status,number_of_nodes,active_shards} confirms a real live cluster (anti-honeypot)
GET /_snapshot (or /_cat/repositories?format=json) -> enumerate repository names + backend type (fs/s3/gcs/azure/url) + settings (bucket/location, NOT the data)
GET /_snapshot/{repo}/_all -> list snapshot names, uuids, state, start_time, and the indices[] array (names only)
GET /_cat/indices?format=json and GET /_aliases -> live index inventory to corroborate the snapshot indices[] (spot .ml-* / *knn* / *embeddings* names)
GET /_mapping (or /{ai-named-index}/_mapping) -> confirm dense_vector / sparse_vector / knn_vector field types = AI-scope gate satisfied
GET /_ml/trained_models (ES) or /_plugins/_ml/models (OpenSearch) and GET /_ingest/pipeline -> deployed embedding/inference models = positive AI attribution
All read-only GETs only; stop at names + metadata
vulnerabilities: CVE-2015-5531: directory traversal in Elasticsearch before 1.6.1 via the snapshot API repository path; unauthenticated remote arbitrary file read with JVM process privileges (Metasploit module exists)
CVE-2014-3120: default dynamic scripting (MVEL) in Elasticsearch before 1.2 allows unauthenticated RCE via the _search API on the same open 9200 surface that exposes /_snapshot
CVE-2015-1427: Groovy scripting sandbox bypass in Elasticsearch 1.3.0-1.3.7/1.4.0-1.4.2 yields unauthenticated RCE on the open REST API alongside the snapshot surface
CVE-2023-31419: unauthenticated StackOverflow DoS via crafted _search query string on the same open HTTP API
CVE-2023-31418: unauthenticated OutOfMemory DoS — a moderate number of malformed HTTP requests forces an Elasticsearch node to exit
CVE-2024-23444: snapshot/repository private key stored on disk unencrypted; authenticated attacker can obtain S3/GCS repository credentials (backup-store pivot)
CVE-2024-52979: uncontrolled resource consumption evaluating crafted Mustache search templates crashes the node (DoS)
